facts.statement: The genus Paraptenodytes was named by Ameghino in 1891.
The genus includes the type species P. antarcticus, P. robustus, and the disputed species P. brodkorbi.
facts.quote: subdivision: P. antarcticus (type) P. robustus P. brodkorbi (disputed)

facts.statement: Former names for the genus include Metancylornis, Isotremornis, and Treleudytes, all proposed by Ameghino in 1905.
facts.quote: synonyms: Metancylornis Ameghino 1905 Isotremornis Ameghino 1905 Treleudytes Ameghino 1905

facts.statement: Fossils of Paraptenodytes date from the Early to Middle Miocene, possibly extending into the Pliocene.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Early-Mid Miocene (Colhuehuapian-Laventan) possibly to Pliocene~

facts.statement: Paraptenodytes was an extinct genus of penguins ranging in size from a Magellanic penguin to an emperor penguin.
facts.quote: Paraptenodytes is an extinct genus of penguins which contains two or three species sized between a Magellanic penguin and an emperor penguin

facts.statement: Fossils of Paraptenodytes were discovered in the Santa Cruz and Chubut Provinces of Patagonia, Argentina.
facts.quote: The fossils were found in the Santa Cruz and Chubut Provinces of Patagonia, Argentina

facts.statement: The fossils come from the Gaiman, Monte León, and Santa Cruz Formations dating to the Early to Middle Miocene.
facts.quote: in the Gaiman, Monte León and Santa Cruz Formations of Early to Middle Miocene age

facts.statement: Paraptenodytes forms the subfamily Paraptenodytinae with Arthrodytes, a group that is not ancestral to modern penguins.
facts.quote: Together with the related genus Arthrodytes, they form the subfamily Paraptenodytinae, which is not an ancestor of modern penguins.

facts.statement: Florentino Ameghino named the genus Paraptenodytes in 1891 for fossils originally described by Moreno and Mercerat as Palaeospheniscus antarcticus.
facts.quote: El género Paraptenodytes fue acuñado por Florentino Ameghino en 1891 para designar a los especímenes fósiles originalmente descritos por François Moreno y Alcide Mercerat como Palaeospheniscus antarcticus.

facts.statement: The holotype of Paraptenodytes antarcticus is deposited in the Museo de La Plata in Argentina.
facts.quote: cuyo holotipo (MLP 20-2, 20-4, 20-6) se encuentra depositado en el Museo de La Plata, Argentina

facts.statement: The holotype specimens of Paraptenodytes antarcticus come from the Monte León Formation of the Early Miocene.
facts.quote: proceden de la Formación Monte León (Mioceno temprano)

facts.statement: George Gaylord Simpson described a new specimen of the type species in 1946, which included associated skull and postcranial parts.
facts.quote: En 1946, George Gaylord Simpson describió un nuevo espécimen de la especie tipo (AMNH 3338), el cual incluía parte del cráneo y postcráneo asociados.

facts.statement: For many years, the specimen described by Simpson was the most complete known fossil penguin skeleton and the only one with an associated skull until Marplesiornis was described in 1960.
facts.quote: Este hallazgo fue durante años el esqueleto de pingüino fósil más completo conocido y en el único con cráneo asociado hasta la descripción de Marplesiornis en 1960.

facts.statement: A second species, Paraptenodytes robustus, has been described, referred to the San Julián Formation of the Eocene-Oligocene.
facts.quote: Existe una segunda especie descrita para el género, Paraptenodytes robustus, referido a la Formación San Julián (Eoceno-Oligoceno)

facts.statement: The holotype of Paraptenodytes robustus is deposited in the Natural History Museum in London, England.
facts.quote: cuyo holotipo (NH A/591) se encuentra depositado en el Natural History Museum de Londres, Inglaterra.

facts.statement: Recent phylogenetic analyses suggest that Paraptenodytes is more closely related to living penguins than to Paleogene giant penguins.
facts.quote: Los análisis filogenéticos recientes sugieren que Paraptenodytes se encuentra más próximo a los pingüinos vivientes que a los pingüinos gigantes del Paleógeno.

facts.statement: The humerus of Paraptenodytes has rounded ventral and dorsal condyles, unlike the elongated ones in Arthrodytes, with a total length between 90 and 150 mm.
facts.quote: condylus ventralis y dorsalis redondeados a diferencia de los de Arthrodytes que son alargados y longitud total entre 90 y 150 mm.

facts.statement: Paraptenodytes belongs to the family Spheniscidae.
Paraptenodytes lived from 23.04 to 15.98 million years ago, during the Aquitanian to Burdigalian stages.
facts.quote: Time range: Aquitanian to Burdigalian (23.04 to 15.98 million years ago)
